output.brief: The Admissions Office is not the main cause of the enrolment drop. Applications and admits both rose, so the pool was not the problem. The yield fall (41.8% to 34.3%) lines up with the new scholarship schedule. Presidential awards were unchanged and their yield stayed flat at about 36%. The no-merit group also stayed flat. Dean's awards fell from $14,000 to $9,000 and Merit awards from $9,000 to $5,000, and yield in those tiers fell about 13 points each. Early-action students got decisions on time on the old system, yet their yield fell by almost the same amount as regular-decision students (7.4 versus 7.5 points). So the late portal decisions don't explain the drop. The delays were real and hurt some individual students, and the missing-transcript complaints are untested. Replacing the director would punish the wrong party and wouldn't fix the cause. I am fairly confident, but the extract doesn't split tiers by round, and the consultant's 2021 price estimate clearly understated the effect. Next steps: take a proposal to the finance committee to restore awards in the Dean's and Merit tiers, with the net-revenue trade-off modelled, before award letters go out. Also set a decision-turnaround target, and check the transcript issue before ordering vendor rework.
